sentences.text:
Mohammed Mustafa Sajid, Hyd., vs The State Of Telangana, Rep
Pp., on 12 June, 2024
 1
 The Honourable Sri Justice E. V. Venugopal
 Criminal Revision Case No.254 Of 2016
O R D E R:

The present Criminal Revision Case is filed against the order dated 14.09.2015 passed in Crl.M.P.No.3910 of 2014 in C.C.No.396 of 2014 on the file of the learned VIII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad, at Rajendranagar (for short, "the trial Court").
2.

entities.text: VIII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad, at Rajendranagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Mr.Mohd.Abdul Quddus, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr.Vizarath Ali, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent-State.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner/accused is the inhabitant of Mallepally,
Hyderabad and the complainant is the Inspector/Exe of C.I.S.F. (Central Industrial Security Force),
RGI Airport, Shamshabad.

entities.text:
C.I.S.F. (Central Industrial Security Force),
RGI Airport,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On 26.06.2012, the complainant gave a written complaint stating that the petitioner was trying to go out from the departure gate of Rajiv Gandhi Airport, Shamshabad and unauthorizedly entered into the terminal building using fake/fabricated/cancelled e-ticket of AI-617 destination to Kolkota at 10:30 hrs.
Basing on the said facts the present case is registered against the petitioner for the offence under Section 420 of I.P.C.

It is further stated that the petitioner filed the discharge petition under Section 239 Cr.P.C. seeking to discharge him for the offence under Section 420 of I.P.C. stating that the ingredients as culled out under Section 420 of I.P.C. are not being attracted against him.
But the trial Court vide impugned order dismissed the discharge petition stating that prima facie case has been made out against the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner filed the present Revision seeking to set aside the impugned order.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the alleged cancelled ticket of the petitioner is neither seized from the petitioner nor filed along with the charge sheet, which itself shows that the prosecution has foisted a false case against him only to harass him.
Therefore, he seeks to set aside the impugned order.
5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submitted that the Officials, upon conducting thorough enquiry had registered the present case against the petitioner and seeks to dismiss the Revision.
6. This Court vide order dated 28.01.2016 granted interim stay of all proceedings in C.C.No.396 of 2014 on the file of the trial Court.
Later, the matter underwent several adjournments.

sentences.text: Having regard to the submissions made by both the learned counsel and relying upon the decision passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others Vs. State of Bihar and Others 1

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others Vs. State of Bihar and Others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , this Court is of the opinion that neither there is any dishonest inducement on the part of the petitioner nor had he deceived any person and received any property to convert to his own use.

Thus, the ingredients as culled out under Section 420 of I.P.C. does not attract against the petitioner herein and it would be unjust if the petitioner is forced to go through the tribulations of the trial.
8. Accordingly, the Criminal Revision Case is allowed by setting aside the order dated 14.09.2015 passed in Crl.M.P.No.3910 of 2014 in C.C.No.396 of 2014.
Miscellaneous Petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
E.V. VENUGOPAL, J Date: 12.06.2024 ESP 1 2022 LawSuit (SC) 149
